items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: And I told him about, you know I said when I was a kid and I sat in with your band, you came up to me after the set I played and you said, “hey kid, you trying to take my job?”

ctx.x: It seems like you’ve had some very fortunate working situations throughout your career that really gave you what you needed for the rest of your career.

Yeah. Well I said I’ve been lucky I’ve been able to play with all the people that I used to look up to when I was a teenager. Like I thought Basie was the greatest thing in life and when I was in the Army, one of the bass players in the Army, Walt Yoder had worked with Woody’s band and he knew all the guys in the Basie band and he took me and the guitar player, my best friend Tony Rizzi, out to the ballroom to see Basie, and he arranged for us to sit in. I mean I’m like 20 years old and Basie’s one of my idols,…

along in the business to avoid any of the pitfalls you might have run into, you should do it. You owe that to this business. Don’t get into racial scenes. I used to be Charlie Shaver’s bodyguard when we did a tour of the south. I mean I would go to the men’s room with him.
